claim: UK IHT: long-term UK resident = UK resident for at least 10 of the previous 20 tax years, from 6 April 2025
evidence: IHTA 1984 s.6A(1) verbatim: 'an individual is a long-term UK resident at all times in a tax year if they were UK resident for at least 10 of the previous 20 tax years'. Inserted by Finance Act 2025 s.44(3)(4), 6.4.2025. gov.uk guidance wording is looser (adds 'consecutive' bullet): use statute wording

claim: Tail after leaving the UK is 3 to 10 tax years depending on years of UK residence
evidence: s.6A(2)-(3): not long-term resident if non-UK resident for any 10 consecutive years in the previous 19, or for the required number of consecutive years. Table: 13 or fewer=3; 14=4; 15=5; 16=6; 17=7; 18=8; 19=9; 20=10. gov.uk guidance and IHTM47020 give the same table

claim: Long-term residents are chargeable on non-UK assets at death or on transfers
evidence: gov.uk: 'if you are a long-term UK resident, your non-UK (overseas) assets may be subject to Inheritance Tax if you make a transfer of assets or die'. Domicile still relevant for events before 6.4.2025, some trusts and treaties that use domicile (IHTM47001)

claim: No UK-Spain inheritance tax treaty
evidence: HMRC list of IHT conventions: Ireland, South Africa, USA, Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland (modern) and France, Italy, India, Pakistan (pre-1975). Spain not listed. Unilateral relief available for similar foreign tax where no agreement

claim: A British person moving to Spain stays within UK IHT on worldwide assets for the tail period
evidence: Derived from s.6A(2)-(3) and the gov.uk example (10 to 13 years of residence = 3 years after leaving)

claim: Spanish succession tax interplay and Valencian bonuses for a UK mover
evidence: Only Ley 29/1987 art. 6 (obligacion personal), art. 23 (credit for foreign tax) and DA 2 (regional rules for non-resident deceased: Community with most Spanish assets) were opened. Valencian bonuses not checked; interplay of UK and Spanish credits is a legal judgement call

claim: IRNR general rate 24 %, 19 % for EU/EEA residents with effective exchange of information (art. 25.1.a TRLIRNR)
evidence: Art. 25.1.a verbatim: 'Con carácter general el 24 por 100. No obstante, el tipo de gravamen será el 19 por ciento cuando se trate de contribuyentes residentes en otro Estado miembro de la Unión Europea o del Espacio Económico Europeo con el que exista un efectivo intercambio de información tributaria'. Last modified 2015 (Ley 26/2014)

claim: Expense deductions only for EU/EEA residents (art. 24.6)
evidence: Art. 24.6 TRLIRNR: for residents in another EU Member State (and EEA with effective information exchange) individuals may deduct IRPF-law expenses directly and inseparably linked to the Spanish income

claim: UK residents are not EU/EEA after the transition period: 24 % and no art. 24.6 deductions for income accrued from 1 Jan 2021
evidence: AEAT Brexit page: 'dejará de ser aplicable el tipo de gravamen general del 19%... pasará a ser aplicable el 24%'; 'No se podrán deducir los gastos previstos en el artículo 24.6'; art. 14 exemptions and art. 46 option end; reinvestment relief on main home ends; treaty 'continuará siendo aplicable'

claim: Rental income of a UK resident: 24 % on gross rent, no expenses
evidence: AEAT Brexit page lists 'rendimientos de inmuebles' and 'renta imputadas de bienes inmuebles' among income taxed at 24 %; art. 24.6 expenses not deductible. Imputed-income percentage (LIRPF art. 85) not opened

claim: Capital gains on Spanish property by a non-resident: 19 % or 24 %?
evidence: Art. 25.1.f.3 TRLIRNR: 19 % for gains on transfers of assets, for every non-resident (not 24 %). Art. 25.2: buyer withholds 3 % of the price on account. Home-reinvestment exemption no longer available to UK residents (AEAT)

claim: Dividends and interest from Spain to a UK resident
evidence: Art. 25.1.f.1-2: 19 % internal rate. Treaty art. 10(2)(a): source-State tax capped at 10 %; art. 11: interest taxable only in residence State. AEAT: interest exempt by invoking the treaty after Brexit

claim: UK counts as EU/EEA under TRLIRNR after the end of the transition period
evidence: No. AEAT: the EU-specific provisions 'dejarán de ser aplicables a los contribuyentes residentes en el Reino Unido una vez finalizado el período transitorio'; the UK-Spain convention remains applicable

claim: Modelo 210 is now an annual grouped return (Orden HAC/623/2026)
evidence: Annual grouping for rents exists since accruals of 2024 (AEAT: 'ha pasado de ser TRIMESTRAL a ANUAL'). Orden HAC/623/2026 (BOE 23.6.2026, in force 24.6.2026) changes deadlines and content: rents with amount to pay 1-20 April of following year (grouped or separate); imputed income 1 April-31 Dec; new expenses annex and days/ownership boxes for returns filed from 1.1.2027

claim: Modelo 210 timing of the new deadlines
evidence: Grouped rents and imputed income: accruals of 2026 (first filing 1-20 April 2027). Separate rent returns: only accruals from Q4 2026; Q2-Q3 2026 keep 20 July and 20 October; imputed income of 2025 keeps 1 Jan-31 Dec 2026. Direct debit 1-15 April, imputed income until 23 Dec. Other income quarterly (20 days of Apr/Jul/Oct/Jan); zero-tax 1-20 Jan; refunds from 1 Feb

claim: Modelo 210 for sale of Spanish property: filed within 3 months after the 1 month following the transfer
evidence: Art. 5.a Orden EHA/3316/2010 as restated by Orden HAC/623/2026 (art. 14.4 Reglamento IRNR)

claim: US-Spain Protocol signed 14 January 2013
evidence: BOE-A-2019-15166: Protocol and Memorandum of Understanding done at Madrid, 14 January 2013 (Montoro / Solomont). IRS page lists the Protocol dated 1-14-2013

claim: Protocol entered into force 27 November 2019
evidence: BOE 23.10.2019 (BOE-A-2019-15166): 'entrarán en vigor el 27 de noviembre de 2019' (3 months after the last note, art. XV). IRS and Treasury pages open do not state the date

claim: Dividends withholding after the Protocol: 5 % (company holding 10 %+), 15 % otherwise, 0 % at 80 %+ and for pension funds
evidence: Protocol art. IV (new art. 10). Before: 10 % (25 % holding) and 15 %. Branch tax art. 14 abolished (art. VIII)

claim: Interest and royalties after the Protocol: taxable only in State of residence
evidence: Protocol arts. V and VI (new arts. 11 and 12). Before: interest 10 %, royalties 5/8/10 %. Exception: US contingent interest capped at 10 % if beneficial owner is Spanish

claim: Savings clause and tie-breaker
evidence: Art. 1(3) savings clause unchanged by the Protocol ('un Estado contratante puede someter a imposición a sus residentes... y por razón de ciudadanía puede someter a imposición a sus ciudadanos, como si el Convenio no hubiese entrado en vigor'); Protocol only adds art. 1(5) GATS and 1(6) transparent entities. Art. 4(2) tie-breaker unchanged (permanent home, vital interests, habitual abode, nationality, MAP)

claim: Pensions and social security: art. 20(2) covers social security payments
evidence: Art. 20(1)(a): pensions for past employment taxable only in State of residence. Art. 20(1)(b): social security benefits paid by a State to a resident of the other State or to a US citizen 'pueden someterse a imposición' in the paying State (not exclusive). Art. 20(2) is annuities. Protocol adds art. 20(5) (pension fund income)

claim: Capital gains art. 13 changed by the Protocol
evidence: Protocol art. VII: 13(4) replaced (gains on shares giving enjoyment of immovable property, taxable where located); 13(6)-(7) merged into new 13(6): other gains only in the transferor's State of residence

claim: 401(k) and IRA are 'pension funds' for treaty purposes
evidence: MoU para. 3(a): US 'fondo de pensiones' includes 401(a)/401(k), 403(b), IRAs (408), Roth IRAs (408A). Spanish tax outcome of withdrawals not verified

claim: US-Spain totalization agreement: signed 30 Sep 1986, in force 1 April 1988
evidence: SSA agreement page: 'Agreement and Administrative Arrangement, both signed at Madrid September 30, 1986. Entered into force April 1, 1988'

claim: Totalization agreement scope: which taxes and benefits it covers
evidence: Art. 2: Spain General System (disability from ordinary illness/non-work injury, old age, death and survivorship) plus special systems; US Title II Social Security Act (except ss. 226, 226A, 228) and IRC 1954 Chapters 2 and 21. Social security contributions and benefits only, no income tax. Art. 4 state-of-work rule, art. 5 five-year detached worker, self-employed by residence

claim: Totalization: certificates, benefit totalling, who pays
evidence: SSA pamphlet: certificate form E/USA 1 via TGSS; US needs 6 credits before Spanish credits count; Spain needs 1 year; each country pays its own benefit

claim: Spanish tax treatment of US Social Security benefits and of 401(k)/IRA withdrawals
evidence: Treaty text only. No AEAT or DGT source opened. IRS and Treasury PDFs are scanned images and unreadable. Escalate

claim: Valencian wealth tax exempt minimum is 2 000 000 EUR from tax year 2026 (Ley 5/2026)
evidence: Ley 5/2026 art. 19 rewrites art. 8 Ley 13/1997: 'La base imponible de los sujetos pasivos por obligación personal del impuesto que residan habitualmente en la Comunitat Valenciana se reduce, en concepto de mínimo exento, en 2.000.000 euros'. BOE 17.9.2026; DOGV 10.8.2026

claim: Effective date 11 August 2026, first applied to wealth at 31 Dec 2026
evidence: Disposicion final quinta: in force the day after DOGV publication (10.8.2026). ATV: '2.000.000 € con efectos desde el 11/08/2026, por lo que afecta al patrimonio del que sea titular a 31/12/2026 (que se declarará en el 2027)'

claim: Earlier values: 500 000 until 2024, 1 000 000 in 2025 (Ley 5/2025)
evidence: ATV table: up to 2024 500 000 (1 000 000 for disability); 2025 1 000 000; from 2026 2 000 000. AEAT 2025 manual: 1 000 000. Text of Ley 5/2025 not opened

claim: The 2 M EUR minimum benefits UK or US owners of Valencian property
evidence: Only Spanish residents in the Comunitat (obligacion personal). LIP art. 28 Tres: the 700 000 EUR minimum applies to non-residents under obligacion personal and to obligacion real. AEAT 2025 manual says the same

claim: State-level exempt minimum is 700 000 EUR
evidence: LIP art. 28 Dos: if the Community has not regulated the minimum, base reduced by 700 000 EUR

claim: Non-residents may apply the regional rules of the Community with the most valuable assets
evidence: LIP DA 4 (Ley 11/2021): all non-residents, not only EU/EEA (AEAT 2025 manual). Whether this combines with the Valencian minimum: not confirmed (manual reads 700 000 EUR)

claim: Wealth tax: non-residents taxed by obligacion real on Spanish assets; accrual 31 December
evidence: LIP art. 5.1.b; ATV 'El impuesto se devenga el 31 de diciembre'

claim: Cuota limit (LIP art. 31) applies to non-residents too
ITSGF status in 2026: 3 M EUR threshold, 700 000 EUR minimum, non-residents included, filed 1-31 July
evidence: Ley 38/2022 art. 3: net wealth above 3 000 000; base reduced 700 000 (also obligacion real, AEAT); same taxpayers as wealth tax; art. 3 prorogued 'en tanto no se produzca la revisión de la tributación patrimonial' (DA 5.2 RDL 8/2023). AEAT: filing 1-31 July; 2025 returns from 1 July 2026. Orden HAC/652/2026 applies the cuota limit to obligacion real. Continuation for 2026 depends on prorogation: re-check

claim: ITSGF filing and 2025 return calendar
evidence: AEAT ITSGF page: model 718 for 2025, filing starts 1 July (2026); 1-31 July of year after accrual; bank debit until 28 July

claim: Wealth tax filing test of 2 000 000 EUR gross assets
evidence: ATV: a return is due if the quota is payable, or if the net base exceeds the minimum and the gross value of assets exceeds 2 000 000 EUR. Interaction not interpreted

claim: Modelo 720 threshold: 50 000 EUR per category
evidence: RGAT art. 42 bis.4.e (accounts: 31 Dec and Q4 average balances, 'conjuntamente'), art. 42 ter.4.c (securities, insurance, annuities); AEAT UK leaflet: no duty per category when it does not exceed 50 000 EUR (real estate included)

claim: Modelo 720 deadline 1 January to 31 March; re-filing only on +20 000 EUR
evidence: RGAT arts. 42 bis.5, 42 ter.5, 42 quater.6. AEAT: 2025 return due 1.1-31.3.2026, plus 4 calendar days for technical failure. 2026 return 1.1-31.3.2027 derived from the RGAT (AEAT 2027 page not published)

claim: CJEU C-788/19 (27 January 2022) ruling
evidence: Operative part verbatim: Spain failed to fulfil obligations under art. 63 TFEU and art. 40 EEA by (1) taxing undeclared assets as 'unjustified capital gains' with no possibility, in practice, of limitation, (2) a proportional 150 % fine concurrent with flat fines, (3) flat fines disproportionate and not capped

claim: Ley 5/2022 changed the Modelo 720 regime
evidence: BOE 10.3.2022, in force 11.3.2022. DF 4 rewrites DA 18 LGT (adds virtual currencies); sole repeal clause repeals DA 1 and 2 Ley 7/2012; DF 5 rewrites art. 39 LIRPF (unjustified gains in the period 'respecto del que se descubran' unless earlier ownership proven)

claim: Penalties for late or missing Modelo 720 after Ley 5/2022
evidence: LGT art. 198: 20 EUR per datum or set of data for one person, minimum 300, maximum 20 000; half if filed late without request. Art. 199 (incomplete or inaccurate): 200 EUR per non-monetary datum; up to 2 % of amounts, minimum 500, for monetary data. Which article applies to a case is a legal judgement call

claim: Old regime: 5 000 EUR per omission, 10 000 minimum, 150 % fine
evidence: Repealed from 11.3.2022 (Ley 5/2022 repeal clause 2). Live EN post 27449 still states '5,000-per-omission': OUTDATED

claim: Modelo 721 for crypto held abroad
evidence: RGAT art. 42 quater (RD 249/2023); Orden HFP/886/2023 (BOE-A-2023-17429, in force 30.7.2023); 50 000 EUR at 31 Dec valued in euros; 1 Jan-31 Mar; coins with non-resident custodians that safeguard private keys for third parties; self-custody wallets excluded (AEAT FAQ). Consistent with data/factcheck/8615.csv

claim: DAC8 and MiCA context for crypto
evidence: Reused from data/factcheck/8615.csv (checked 2026-10-02): DAC8 collection from 1 Jan 2026, no Spanish transposition in BOE at that date. Not re-opened today

claim: UK pension plans are not reported on Modelo 720 before a contingency
evidence: DGT V0890-24: rights in a foreign pension plan are not in any 720 category until a contingency occurs, unless the plan gives a surrender right like a life policy (art. 42 ter.3.a)

claim: UK ISA holdings are reportable on Modelo 720
evidence: Not checked; no DGT ruling found. Do not state

claim: UK-Spain Convention 2013: signed London 14 March 2013, in force 12 June 2014
evidence: HMRC treaty page: in force 12 June 2014; BOE 15.5.2014 (BOE-A-2014-5171). Synthesised text with MLI (2023 effects): MLI makes no change to arts. 17 and 18

claim: Art. 17: private pensions taxable only in the State of residence
evidence: HMRC English: 'Subject to the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 18, pensions and other similar remuneration paid to an individual who is a resident of a Contracting State, shall be taxable only in that State.' AEAT: pension for past private employment taxed only in Spain

claim: Art. 18(2): government service pensions
evidence: Taxable only in the paying State unless the individual is both resident and national of the other State (then only there). AEAT: exempt with progression in Spain (DA 20 LIRPF) for a non-Spanish national. Art. 18(3) returns pensions for a State's business activity to art. 17

claim: UK State Pension falls under art. 17 and is taxed only in Spain
evidence: DGT V2460-21 and V1380-25 treat the UK state pension as a public pension under art. 18.2 ('de acuerdo con los escasos datos aportados', paid from funds created for services to the UK Government): British national resident in Spain taxed only in UK, exempt with progression in Spain; Spanish national taxed only in Spain. Escalate

claim: SIPP and workplace pensions: art. 17, taxed only in Spain
evidence: AEAT leaflet covers pensions 'por razón de un empleo anterior en el sector privado'. Not confirmed for SIPPs (personal pensions)

claim: UK 25 % tax-free lump sum: Spanish treatment
evidence: Art. 17 silent on lump sums. LIRPF art. 17.2.a).3 makes plan benefits employment income; art. 18.3 30 % reduction only for art. 17.2.a) 1 and 2; DT 12 keeps old 40 % relief only for contributions up to 2006 within short windows. No primary source on the UK lump sum (V3375-15 concerns a pension). Secondary sources not accepted

claim: Treaty articles for UK investors: dividends, interest, gains, relief
evidence: Art. 10(2)(a) 10 % cap; art. 11 interest residence only; art. 13(1) real estate gains taxable where located; art. 13(6) other gains residence only; art. 22 credit relief in Spain; art. 2(3) covered UK taxes: income tax, corporation tax, CGT

claim: Convention contains no provision on UK ISAs
evidence: Searched the BOE Spanish text and the HMRC English PDF for 'ISA' and 'Individual Savings': no match

claim: Spain taxes ISA income and gains as ordinary savings income
evidence: Follows from arts. 10, 11, 13(6) and absence of an ISA clause, but no AEAT or DGT statement found (DGT database searches returned nothing). Live post 27449 states it as fact: Félix and Sonia to confirm

claim: Live post 27449: UK dividends carry 0 % UK withholding
evidence: Outside the six points; not checked against HMRC
